Subject Arrest of communists in the French Concession; article appearing
in the Central China Daily News.

Made by D.P.S. Henchman. Forwarded by J. Keyes D.S.S

With reference to the attached translation of an article
published in the Central China Daily News, I have to state
that the French Authorities have been visited and, in an
interview, gave the following explanation of the events
referred to in the above mentioned newspaper:-

On 7th November 1936 at the corner of Boulevard de
Montigny and Tsai Sz Road, French Concession, a Chinese
policeman attached to the French Police was requested by an
agent of the Public Safety Bureau to arrest one Li Yang
Ching (李揚清) whom he, the agent, suspected of being a
communist. The Chinese Policeman arrested Li and took him
to the Poste Joffre. Li was arraigned before the court and
during the period of remand, he implicated one Yui Yung Li
(余永礼), a clerk of the Shanghai 2nd Special District Court,
who, in accordance with instructions from the 3rd Branch
Kiangsu High Court, was subsequently arrested. Li was handed
over to the Chinese authorities but before he was handed over
he made a statement to the French Police. In this statement
a number of addresses in the Settlement were mentioned and
enquiries regarding them were instituted, enquiries which
have proved fruitless.

The French Police have so far been unable to obtain further
information regarding the two accused and they have not been
permitted to interrogate Yui; they state that the Chinese authorities
are very secretive about the matter but that they, the French
Police, are of the opinion that Yui, the second person to be
arrested, gave information in the first case which led to Li's
arrest. A copy of Li's statement is herewith attached.

D.C. (Special Branch)
D. P. S.
Henchman

事由 法租界共产党人被捕；《华中日报》刊登之文章。

呈报人：特务科警佐 Henchman。转呈人：副巡官 J. Keyes

关于附译的《华中日报》所刊文章，本人谨陈述如下：经拜访法国当局，其在面谈中就上述报纸所述事件作出如下解释：

1936年11月7日，在法租界蒙蒂尼路（Boulevard de Montigny）与蔡司路（Tsai Sz Road）转角处，一名隶属于法国警察局的华捕应公共安全局一名探员的要求，逮捕了一名李扬清（Li Yang Ching），该探员怀疑其为共产党员。华捕逮捕了李并将其带至霞飞路捕房（Poste Joffre）。李被提堂受审，在还押候审期间，他供出了上海第二特区法院的一名书记员余永礼（Yui Yung Li）。随后，根据江苏高等法院第三分院的指令，余永礼被捕。李被移交给中国当局，但在移交前，他向法国警方作了一份供词。在这份供词中，提到了租界内的一些地址，并就此展开了调查，但调查结果一无所获。

法国警方迄今未能获得关于这两名被告的进一步信息，且未获准审讯余永礼；他们称中国当局对此事讳莫如深，但法国警方认为，第二名被捕者余永礼提供了导致李扬清被捕的第一案线索。兹附上李扬清供词副本一份。

特务科助理总监
特务科警佐
Henchman

Yungkang (永康) and Kinghwa(金華), with a position on
the organisation bureau of this committee. I succeeded in
creating in 1929 and 1930 about ten communist cells in the
above mentioned districts, particularly in the 3rd. district
of Eastern Kinghwa.
In July 1930, the Central Committee of the Chinese
Communist Party instructed two of its members - FANG SHAN
(方山) (NOTE:she surrendered to the Government in 1928)
and LIN'J (林) - to reorganise the political service of the
13th. Red Army under CHENG JEN MOW (程仁模), which at
this time was operating in the neighbourhoods of Tsingyun(云),
Sienku (仙居) and Yungkang(永康). Through the efforts of
one YING KING TSA (應慶寺), I was made a member of the
Army's Communist political service sub-prefectural committee
of Yungkang. This service was under the command of HU
SHANG HUNG (胡双洪). I was instructed to be in charge of
the printing of communist propaganda and literature.
In January 1931, after the defeat of the 13th. Red
Army, I arrived in Shanghai with LIU CHI TAN. In March,
LIU had me go to work as a worker in the Yong Yu Mill (永裕),
Jesuit Road. At the same time I became a member of the
communist cell which existed in the mill. I was instructed
to spread propaganda among the workers. I left this mill
at its closure in January 1932, with the incidence of the
local Sino-Japanese hostilities.
In February 1932 General TSAI TING KAI (蔡廷楷),
Commander of the 19th. Route Army, instructed his friend
CHANG HSUAN (張煊), a member of the Chinese Communist
Party, to form a corps of anti-Japanese volunteers. In this
connection CHANG HSUAN sent LIU CHI TAN and YING KING TSA
to Chekiang, where it was their duty to recruit former soldiers
of the 13th. Red Army. LIU proposed that I went with him.
Mid-February YING KING TSA (in charge), LIU CHI TAN,
CHU CHIEN HAO (朱劍豪), a member of the Wuyi Communist
sub-prefectural committee, WANG TSHING HW/ (王振華), former

1936年11月10日法国警方在法国警察总部从李扬敬（LI YANG KING）处取得的供词译本。

案件编号 CXXXIII

逮捕编号 86

供词由法国警方政治科侦探警佐 J. PERIE 取得，翻译 Andre TSEU 担任口译。

囚犯：李扬敬（LI YANG KING，即李揚敬）。
------

问：你的姓名、职业、出生地及居住地为何？
答：我叫李扬敬（LI YANG KING），又名陈光明（ZENG KWANG MING，原文如此，应为音译差异），浙江人，无业。我居住在熙华德路（Route de Sieyes）荣福里7号。我今年25岁。
问：你加入中国共产党多久了？
答：我最初在养元（Yang Yuan）小学读书，后来继续在金华（Kinghwa）的灵麓（Ling Yor）中学就读。1927年，当我16岁时，在我仍在养元学校就读期间，通过金华东区第三区委员楼其潭（LIU CHI TAN）的努力和介绍，我加入了共产主义青年团。（注：楼于1934年在浙江温州被捕，不久后死于杭州监狱。）我是由养元学校的一名教师应计周（YING CHI CHOU）介绍给楼的。加入共产主义青年团两年后（1929年），我以李康白（LI KANG PAI）的名字，再次通过楼其潭的介绍，加入了中国共产党，并成为永康（Yungkang）和金华（Kinghwa）的区委委员，在该委员会的组织局任职。我在1929年和1930年间，在上述地区，特别是金华东区第三区，成功建立了约十个共产党小组。
1930年7月，中共中央指示其两名成员——方山（FANG SHAN）（注：她于1928年向政府自首）和林（LIN'J）——重组程仁模（CHENG JEN MOW）率领的红十三军的政治部，该军当时在缙云（Tsingyun，原文不清，推测为缙云或青田等地）、仙居（Sienku）和永康（Yungkang）附近活动。通过应庆寺（YING KING TSA，音译）的努力，我成为红十三军驻永康县政治部 Subcommittee（分会/支委）的成员。该政治部由胡双洪（HU SHANG HUNG）指挥。我受命负责印刷共产党的宣传品和文献。
1931年1月，红十三军失败后，我与楼其潭抵达上海。3月，楼让我去耶稣会路（Jesuit Road）的永裕纱厂（Yong Yu Mill）当工人。同时，我成为了该厂存在的共产党小组的成员。我受命在工人中开展宣传工作。1932年1月，随着当地中日敌对行动（一·二八事变）的发生，该厂关闭，我也离开了那里。
1932年2月，第十九路军指挥官蔡廷楷（TSAI TING KAI，原文如此，通常为蔡廷锴）将军指示他的朋友、中共党员张煊（CHANG HSUAN）组建一支抗日义勇军。为此，张煊派遣楼其潭和应庆寺前往浙江，他们的任务是招募红十三军的退伍士兵。楼提议我与他同行。2月中旬，由应庆寺（负责人）、楼其潭、武义共产党县委委员朱剑豪（CHU CHIEN HAO）、前红十三军第一团团长王振华（WANG TSHING HW/，原文残缺，推测为王振华）以及我自己组成的队伍，经过浙江，离开上海两天后经杭州抵达金华。到达金华车站时，朱剑豪和王振华被保安团成员逮捕，因为在他们身上发现了“中国国民党抗日志愿军”的徽章。

pages.en:
- 2 -

commander of the 1st. regiment of the 13th. Red Army, and
myself, passed through Chekiang and arrived in Kinghwa via
Hangchow two days after leaving Shanghai. Arriving at King-
hwa Station, CHU CHIEN HAO and WANG TSENG HWA were arrested
by members of the Peace Preservation Corps, because in their
possession had been found badges of the "Anti-Japanese Volun-
teers' Army of the Chinese Kuomintang Party" (中國國民黨抗日志願軍).
They were taken to the Kinghwa Peace Preservation Corps' HQS
and later transferred to Hangchow, where they were sentenced
to two months' imprisonment each for the usurpation of public
functions. The authorities did not then realise that they
had communists to deal with.
Two days after their arrest, LIU and I returned to
Shanghai, whilst YING left for Yungkang in order to work there
in the organising of the volunteers' army.
In Shanghai we put up at the Hung Ziang (鴻祥),
Hotel, Avenue Road. LIU informed the Central Committee of
the Chinese Communist Party, which was then in Shanghai, of
the arrest of our two comrades. We stayed at the Hung Ziang
Hotel for about ten days after which I removed to No. 13
Long Tsang Li (隆昌里), Connaught Road, where a room was
rented for me by LIU. Towards the end of March LIU intro-
duced me to the Western Shanghai district Committee of the
C.C.P. This move was really only a matter of form, for in
reality I was working for LIU personally, who was a member
of the Special Corps (G.P.U.) of the C.C.Party.
My first assignment was the transmission on August
7 or 8, of certain communist documents handed me by LIU, to
one TSANG TEH FOU (張德孚), secretary of the Communist
Paoshan sub-prefectural committee. On another occasion -
April 19 - I, accompanied by three comrades, two of whom were
armed with automatic pistols, proceeded to the Yangtsepoo
district. Near Kou Ka Za (顧家宅), I saw a large gathering
of foreign and Chinese policemen. Frightened, I returned
to the meeting place - Tsung Shan Road (中山路橋) Bridge,
where I met my comrades, who explained that they were armed
in order to intervene, should it be necessary, in the dispute
between the management and the workers of the three mills on
strike. These mills were the Yu Tai (豫泰), Wei Ming
(偉明), and another the name of which I have forgotten.
Q. Being a member of the C.C.P. you should know full well, that
by order of the IIIrd. International, members of the communist
party have no right to carry arms in the course of meetings or
manifestations.
A. I did not know that. I simply executed the orders I received.
On May 5 I left Shanghai taking certain communist documents
to one named LING KIANG (林江), of the Wu Shan (湖山小學)
Primary School, Tungchow.
Q. At what time during the day did you leave Shanghai for Tungchow?
A. In the evening.
Q. Do you know what happened in Shanghai on the morning of May 5?
A. No.
Q. Have you heard of the Hongkew Park outrage?
A. I learnt of it after my return from Tungchow on May 7.
Q. Are you certain of that?
A. Yes, of course: I learnt of this news on May 7 after my return
from Tungchow.
Q. You're a liar, because the Hongkew Park outrage took place on
March 31, when you were in Shanghai, and you must have heard
people speak about the affair or read the news of it in the
newspapers.
A. Yes. I was telling lies just now; I had heard of this out-
rage prior to leaving for Tungchow.
Q. Why did you lie?
A. Lack of memory.
Q. What was your second assignment?
A. In about June, I took certain documents to Soochow for the
Wu Hsien Jih Pao (吳縣日報). I handed them to the editor
of this newspaper - one named KIANG SIAO POU (江筱波).
pages.zh:
- 2 -

他们被带到金华保安队总部，随后被转送至杭州，因冒充公职人员罪各被判处两个月监禁。当局当时并未意识到他们是在对付共产党员。
在他们被捕两天后，楼和我返回上海，而应则前往永康，在那里从事义勇军的组织工作。
在上海，我们住在爱文义路（Avenue Road）的鸿祥（Hung Ziang，音译）旅馆。楼将我们两名同志被捕的情况通知了当时在上海的中共中央。我们在鸿祥旅馆住了大约十天，之后我搬到了康纳脱路（Connaught Road）隆昌里13号，这是楼为我租的房间。3月底，楼将我介绍给中共上海西区区委。这一举动实际上只是形式上的，因为实际上我是直接为楼工作，他是中共特科（G.P.U.，原文如此，指特别行动组/特工部门）的成员。
我的第一项任务是在8月7日或8日，将楼交给我的某些共产党文件传递给中共宝山县委秘书张德孚（TSANG TEH FOU）。另一次——4月19日，我在三名同志的陪同下前往杨树浦（Yangtsepoo）区，其中两人配有自动手枪。在顾家宅（Kou Ka Za）附近，我看到大量外国和华人警察聚集。我感到害怕，便返回集合地点——中山路桥（Tsung Shan Road Bridge），在那里遇到了我的同志们，他们解释说，他们携带武器是为了在必要时干预三家罢工工厂的管理层与工人之间的纠纷。这三家工厂是豫泰（Yu Tai）、伟明（Wei Ming），另一家的名字我忘记了。
问：身为中共党员，你应该很清楚，根据第三国际的命令，共产党员在会议或示威活动中无权携带武器。
答：我不知道这一点。我只是执行我收到的命令。
5月5日，我离开上海，将某些共产党文件带给通州（Tungchow）湖山小学（Wu Shan Primary School，音译）的一位名叫林江（LING KIANG）的人。
问：你是当天什么时间离开上海前往通州的？
答：晚上。
问：你知道5月5日上午上海发生了什么事吗？
答：不知道。
问：你听说过虹口公园爆炸案吗？
答：我是5月7日从通州回来后才知道的。
问：你确定吗？
答：是的，当然：我是5月7日从通州回来后得知这个消息的。
问：你在撒谎，因为虹口公园爆炸案发生在3月31日，当时你在上海，你肯定听到人们谈论此事或在报纸上读到过相关新闻。
答：是的。我刚才在撒谎；在前往通州之前，我就听说过这起爆炸案。
问：你为什么撒谎？
答：记性不好。
问：你的第二项任务是什么？
答：大约在6月，我带了一些文件去苏州，交给《吴县日报》（Wu Hsien Jih Pao）。我将文件交给了该报编辑——一位名叫江筱波（KIANG SIAO POU）的人。

pages.en:
- 3 -

I stayed four days in Soochow.
I then returned to Shanghai, but LIU having left for Wenchow (Chekiang), I lost all touch with the Communist Party.
In June 1932 I met HU JEN CHI (胡岩些), a member of the Yungkang Communist sub-prefectural committee, of which I had been a member.
HU YEN CHI had come to see my sister HSIANG CHU (香珠), married to a certain SHA MING (宅明), who at that time was living in the Yong Yu (永裕) Mill, Kwang Fu Road (光復號), Chapei. At present she resides and works at the Sing Sing Mill, Tseu Kia Chiao (周家桥? 沙廠).
On the orders of HU YEN CHI, I again left for Yungkang towards the end of June, in order to reorganise the sub-prefectural committee of this locality.
On arrival there, the members of the former committee got together again to establish reorganisation bases.
We succeeded in reorganising it, and in November 1932 I was sent, in company with CHENG YI CHENG (程義人) and CHENG AH NING (程阿銀), to Sienku (仙居), to reorganise a detachment of bandits and to rally them under the communist standard.
We succeeded in thus forming an independent regiment, known as the "Eastern Chekiang Independent Regiment."
Q. Were you in touch with FANG TSE MING (方志敏)?
A. Yes; the regiment was placed under the command of LAI TSUNG (雷震). I was transferred to the bureau of the political commissar of this regiment on instructions from one TING KING YUNG (丁金榮). We were fighting nearly every day with the Chekiang Peace Preservation Corps. In April 1933 300 of our men surrendered to the Government; the others, about 200, dispersed and became bandits. I returned alone to Yungkang. On My arrival, I went to locate one HUANG LING PIAO (黄齡標), liaison agent of the sub-prefectural committee of this town, and was ordered to reorganise the auxiliary groupings of the C.C.P. in Yungkang.
In July 1933 four members of the Yungkang sub-prefectural committee were arrested by the Police; I was able to get away because at the time of the Police raid I was absent buying something or other. With the disappearance of the committee, liaison with the Central Committee was cut, and I made my way to Yusien (油仙) near Yungkang, where I found asylum in the communist cell of this town. I remained there until September 1933 when I left for Shanghai, where I stayed with my sister who was residing at the Yong Yu No. 2 Mill.
I remained unemployed, vainly trying to get in touch with the Central Committee.
In October 1934 I was married to a work-girl named HU YEH MAN (胡岩些); she was employed at the Yong Yu Mill; she did not wish me to take up my communistic activities again, but provided for my needs; she earned 40 dollars a month.
However, some days after my marriage I was arrested at Sio Sio Dou (Jessfield) by a detective of the Bureau of Public Safety. My former comrades had denounced me. I was interrogated in Shanghai and then transferred to Hangchow, whence I was sent to Yungkang (Chekiang), from where I succeeded in escaping during the course of a fire on April 17, 1935.
Q. On what date were you transferred to Hangchow?
A. The 21st. of the 11th. moon. I was imprisoned in this town until the 26th. of the 1st. moon of the 24th. year, when I was sent to the Yungkang authorities. I remained there until the 16th. of the 4th. moon; on this night, a fire broke out near the prison, and profiting from these
pages.zh:
- 3 -

我在苏州停留了四天。
随后我返回上海，但由于刘（LIU）已前往温州（浙江），我与共产党失去了所有联系。
1932年6月，我遇到了胡岩些（HU JEN CHI），他是永康县委委员，我也曾是该委员会的成员。
胡岩些（HU YEN CHI）是来看望我的妹妹香珠（HSIANG CHU）的，她嫁给了一个叫宅明（SHA MING）的人，当时住在闸北光復號永裕纱厂。目前她居住在周家桥? 沙廠的新新纱厂并在那里工作。
根据胡岩些（HU YEN CHI）的命令，我在6月底再次前往永康，以重组该地的县委。
到达那里后，前委员会的成员重新聚集，建立重组基础。
我们成功进行了重组，1932年11月，我与程義人（CHENG YI CHENG）和程阿銀（CHENG AH NING）一同被派往仙居（Sienku），去重组一股匪帮，并将他们召集到共产主义旗帜下。
我们成功组建了一个独立团，称为“浙东独立团”。
问：你与方志敏（FANG TSE MING）有联系吗？
答：是的；该团归雷震（LAI TSUNG）指挥。根据丁金榮（TING KING YUNG）的指示，我被调任该团政治委员办事处。我们几乎每天都与浙江保安团作战。1933年4月，我方300人向政府投降；其余约200人四散成为匪徒。我独自返回永康。到达后，我去寻找该镇县委的联络员黄齡標（HUANG LING PIAO），并受命重组中共在永康的辅助组织。
1933年7月，永康县委的四名成员被警察逮捕；我得以逃脱，因为在警察突袭时我外出购买物品。随着委员会的消失，与中央委员会的联系中断，我前往永康附近的油仙（Yusien），在该镇的共产党小组中寻求庇护。我在那里一直待到1933年9月，随后前往上海，与住在永裕二厂的妹妹住在一起。
我处于失业状态，徒劳地试图与中央委员会取得联系。
1934年10月，我与一名名叫胡岩些（HU YEH MAN）的女工结婚；她在永裕纱厂工作；她不希望我重新从事共产主义活动，但供养我的生活；她每月收入40美元。
然而，婚后几天，我在小沙渡（Jessfield）被公共安全局的一名侦探逮捕。我以前的同志告发了我。我在上海受到审讯，随后被转送至杭州，又从杭州被送往永康（浙江），1935年4月17日，趁发生火灾之机，我成功逃脱。
问：你是哪一天被转送至杭州的？
答：十一月二十一日。我被囚禁在该镇直到二十四年一月二十六日，当时我被移交给永康当局。我在那里一直待到四月十六日；当晚，监狱附近发生火灾，利用这些

pages.en:
- 4 -

circumstances, about sixty prisoners and myself succeeded
in escaping. The majority of these prisoners were former
members of the 13th. Army.
I succeeded in fleeing to the neighbourhood of Yusien
(油仙), near Yungkang, where sometime previously, I had
organised the district committee of the Chinese Communist
Party.
I took refuge in the home of one HU HWEI LING (胡威靈),
chief of this committee. He introduced me to the military
committee of the Eastern Chekiang Red Independent Regiment.
This committee had succeeded in reconstituting after
the disbandment of the Chekiang Independent Regiment, four
detachments, comprising about 400 men.
Through the medium of HU HWEI LING I was attached to
the 2nd. detachment as a political commissar. I remained
in this position up till the 8th. moon of the 24th.
year.
My detachment operated in the Tungyang (東陽) and
Yungkang districts.
During this period, we fought three times against the
local militia. During the course of one of these engage-
ments, we succeeded in disarming our enemies.
A company of the 7th. Red Army under LIU YING (刘英),
passed through our district towards the 8th. moon on its
way to Wenchow.
At my request the military committee authorised me to
follow this company.
I therefore left for Wenchow as well as WANG FENG HSIANG
(王凤祥), ex-chief of the 2nd. detachment of the
Eastern Chekiang Independent Regiment.
We arrived at Tsingtien (青田), near Wenchow,
towards the middle of the 9th. moon, and we attempted to
join the Red troops of FANG TSE MING, but as the road was
barred by government troops, I returned with WANG FENG
HSIANG to Yungkang.
After my return, I took up my functions as political
commissar of the 2nd. detachment of the Eastern Chekiang
Independent Regiment.
Q. Were you well armed and equipped?
A. Our 4 detachments possessed 1 machine gun, 5 automatic rifles,
and about 200 rifles and pistols. Personally I was
armed with a Mauser.
Q. What is the role of a political commissar in the course of
combat?
A. He remains at the rear of the troops in order to watch the
fight and to prevent the flight of certain of the fighters.
Several times I fired in order to intimidate them, but I
never fired on Government troops.
Q. You are accused of having assassinated on August 1, 1935,
HUANG SHANG MING (黄尚敏), and six members of his
family.
A. It was not me or men of my detachment who did this crime;
it was the members of the 1st. detachment; this murder
was committed in the locality of Wuping (武平区), near
Yungkang.
We stayed at Yungkang for about three months - that is
up till December 1935.
During this time I was taking a course of political
instruction at Yungkang.
In January 1936 our Red detachments organised organised
gurella warfare in the region of Yungkang; this lasted
three months. We avoided fighting with the larger part of
the government troops, but nevertheless fought eight battles.
Personally, I did not take part in any of these engagements,
as I was staying at Yungkang, detached to the military
committee (Staff Major of the Regiment).
I left Yungkang on the 2nd. of the 4th. moon for Shanghai,
because I hoped to establish liaison with the Central Committee
of the Chinese Communist Party, to which I had to submit a
pages.zh:
- 4 -

情况，大约六十名囚犯和我成功
逃脱。这些囚犯大多数是前第十三军
成员。
我成功逃至永康附近的油仙
（Yusien）地区，此前不久，我曾
在那里组织了中国共产党区委员会。
我躲藏在该委员会负责人胡威靈
（HU HWEI LING）家中。他把我引荐
给浙东红军独立团的军事委员会。
在浙江独立团解散后，该委员会
成功重建了四个分队，共计约400人。
通过胡威靈的介绍，我被任命为
第二分队的政治委员。我一直担任
此职直到二十四年八月。
我的分队在东陽（Tungyang）和
永康地区活动。
在此期间，我们与当地民团交战
三次。在其中一次战斗中，我们成
功缴获了敌人的武器。
刘英（LIU YING）率领的红军第七
军团的一个连，大约在八月间经过
我区前往温州。
应我的请求，军事委员会批准我
跟随该连。
因此，我和浙东独立团第二分队
前队长王凤祥（WANG FENG HSIANG）
一同前往温州。
我们在九月月中旬到达温州附近
的青田（Tsingtien），试图加入方
志敏的红军部队，但由于道路被政
府军封锁，我与王凤祥返回永康。
回来后，我恢复了浙东独立团第
二分队的政治委员职务。
问：你们的武装和装备精良吗？
答：我们的四个分队拥有1挺机枪、5支自
动步枪，以及约200支步枪和手枪。
我个人配备了一支毛瑟枪。
问：政治委员在战斗中的作用是什么？
答：他留在部队后方，以监视战斗并防
止某些战士逃跑。我曾多次开枪以
威慑他们，但我从未向政府军开枪。
问：你被指控于1935年8月1日谋杀了
黄尚敏（HUANG SHANG MING）及其六
名家庭成员。
答：实施这一罪行的不是我或我分队的
成员；而是第一分队的成员；这起
谋杀案发生在永康附近的武平区
（Wuping）。
我们在永康停留了大约三个月——即
直到1935年12月。
在此期间，我在永康参加政治训练
班。
1936年1月，我们的红军分队在永康
地区组织了游击战；持续了三个月。
我们避免与大部分政府军交战，但
仍进行了八次战斗。
我个人没有参与任何这些战斗，因
为我留在永康，被派往军事委员会
（团部参谋）。
我于四月二日离开永康前往上海，
因为我希望与中国共产党中央委员
会建立联系，我必须向其提交一份

pages.en:
- 5 -

report on the subject of preparations made by the Reds to
meet a machine gun company of the Government troops, which
had been sent from Hangchow to Tsingyuan (缙云), near
Yungkang.
On arrival at Shanghai on the 4th. of the 4th. moon,
I stayedat the Jui Yu (瑞裕) Hotel, Rue Palikao.
I then went to locate a certain WANG KING CHENG (王景成),
who at this time was residing at the Ying Tah Van (应大房),
Cutlery Shop, Sinza Road. He gave me the address of
YU YUNG LI (俞永礼), a former member of the Yungkang
Communist Prefectural Committee of 1929 and 1930, of whom I
had lost trace. I went straight to the home of YU YUNG
LI, who was residing at the corner of Pere Froc-Rue du
Marche; I forget the exact number. I asked him if he was
still in touch with the Central Committee of the C.C.P.,
but he stated that he was employed in the 2nd. District
Court and had terminated his communistic activities, but
that he would endeavour to locate for me the liaison agent
of the Central Committee of the C.C.P. and would hand him
all documents passed to him for delivery.
Therefore in mid-May I handed him at his home at 7 a.m
one morning, the report made by the Military Committee
regarding the machine gun company, of which I have spoken
higher.
Three days after, YU YUNG LI handed me a receipt on
which was written:
"Received from CHENG YING CHOU (程营週),
"president of the Military Committee of the
"Eastern Chekiang Independent Regiment, one
"report.
Signed:
The C.C. of the C.C.P.1936.
F.S."
Q. What does F.S. mean?
A. I do not know, it is an agreed sign. I instructed one
CHEN HAI WEN (陈海文), liaison agent between me and
the Yungkang sub-prefectural committee, to deliver the
receipt to the members of this committee.
Q. That role does CHEN HAI WEN play and how did you find
him in Shanghai?
A. He is a liaison agent that I had known since 1930. He
was living at the Ying Yung Cheng (应永顺) Foundry,
Tungchow Road. He often went to the Hu Tsen Sang
(胡振昌), Exchange Shop on Yochow Road.
Q. On what date did you send this receipt?
A. Towards the end of May.
Q. When did you see Yu Yung Li for the second time and what
was the object of your conversation?
A. The first time was a simple meeting; the second time
I gave him my report. The third time we wnet to take
food about midday; I forget at which restaurant it was, but
it was located on rue Bluntschli.
Q. How did you live - what were your means of existence?
A. I had $50 that the Military Committee had given me and I had
some money of my own - about $170.
In June 1936 there arrived in Shanghai five members
of the Military Committee of the Chekiang Independent Reg-
iment, of which WANG FENG HSIANG was the commander of the
2nd. detachment of the Regiment; they stayed at the Jui
Yu (瑞裕) and Ming Lo (民乐) Hotels on Rue Palikao.
Their mission was to verify the authenticity of the receipt
delivered to them and to try to get in touch for future
events with the Central Committee of the C.C.P.
These five persons were: WANG FENG HSIANG (王凤祥),
commander of the 2nd. detachment, WANG TSE WU (王子和),
LU TSENG TUNG (芦振东), CHENG LING (陈琳), who was an
officer of the 2nd. detachment, and another whose name I
have forgotten, but he was the father of WANG FENG HSIANG.
pages.zh:
- 5 -

关于红军为应对从杭州派往永康附
近缙云（Tsingyuan）的一支政府军
机枪连所做准备的报告。
四月四日抵达上海后，我住在帕克
路（Rue Palikao）的瑞裕（Jui Yu）
旅馆。
随后我去寻找一个叫王景成（WANG
KING CHENG）的人，他当时住在新闸
路（Sinza Road）的应大房（Ying
Tah Van）刀剪店。他给了我俞永礼
（YU YUNG LI）的地址，俞是1929
年和1930年永康县委的前成员，我
曾与他失去联系。我直接去了俞永
礼的家，他住在神父街（Pere Froc）
与市场路（Rue du Marche）的转角
处；我忘记了确切门牌号。我问他
是否仍与中共中央保持联系，但他
表示他在第二特区法院任职，已终
止共产主义活动，但他会尽力为我
寻找中共中央的联络员，并将交给他
转递的所有文件移交给他。
因此，在五月中旬的一天早上7点，
我在他家中交给了上述提到的关于
机枪连的军事委员会报告。
三天后，俞永礼交给我一张收据，
上面写着：
“收到浙东独立团军事委员会
主席程营週（CHENG YING CHOU）
提交的报告一份。
签名：
中共中央 1936.
F.S.”
问：F.S.是什么意思？
答：我不知道，这是一个约定符号。我指
示陈海文（CHEN HAI WEN），即我与
永康县委之间的联络员，将收据送
给该委员会的成员。
问：陈海文扮演什么角色，你是如何
在上海找到他的？
答：他是我自1930年以来就认识的联络
员。他住在通州路（Tungchow Road）
的应永顺（Ying Yung Cheng）铸造
厂。他经常去耀州路（Yochow Road）
的胡振昌（Hu Tsen Sang）兑换店。
问：你是哪一天发送这张收据的？
答：五月底左右。
问：你第二次见到俞永礼是什么时候，
谈话的目的是什么？
答：第一次只是简单见面；第二次我给
了他我的报告。第三次我们大约在
中午一起去吃饭；我忘记是在哪家
餐馆，但它位于白利南路（rue
Bluntschli）。
问：你是如何生活的——你的生活来
源是什么？
答：我有军事委员会给我的50美元，还
有一些自己的钱——大约170美元。
1936年6月，浙江独立团军事委员会
的五名成员抵达上海，其中王凤祥
是该团第二分队的指挥官；他们住
在帕克路的瑞裕（Jui Yu）和民乐
（Ming Lo）旅馆。
他们的任务是核实交付给他们的收
据的真实性，并尝试就未来事宜与
中共中央取得联系。
这五个人是：第二分队指挥官王凤
祥（WANG FENG HSIANG）、王子和
（WANG TSE WU）、芦振东（LU TSENG
TUNG）、第二分队军官陈琳（CHENG
LING），以及另一个我忘记名字的人，
他是王凤祥的父亲。

pages.en:
-, 6 -

They stayed in Shanghai for about three weeks.
With the arrival of these five in Shanghai, I wrote a
letter to YU YUNG LI, informing him of their presence in
Shanghai.
Three days after the arrival of these representatives
YU YUNG LI came to their hotel, where in my presence he was
given documents of the military committee for transmission
to the Central Committee of the C.C.P. YU YUNG LI left
the hotel, and I do not know whether or not the documents
were safely delivered.
Q. When did you see YU YUNG LI again?
A. Ten days after he had been given the above mentioned papers
I met him in the Ming Loh Hotel in a room occupied by
WANG FENG HSIANG, when he asked in what manner he could
send documents to Yungkang that had emanated from the
Central Committee of the C.C.P. concerning the reorganisation
of the four red detachments, which are mentioned above.
I said that one CHENG LING could always undertake this
mission.
About 4 a.m. the same day, YU YUNG LI brought the
documents and I handed them to CHENG LING, who immediately
left for Yungkang. These events took place at the end of
June and the beginning of July.
The day following the handing over of these documents,
YU YUNG LI rented a room on Rue du Moulin, at the home of
the proprietor of the Shing Hsiang Tsa (馨香斋)
Bakery, in order that WANG FENG HSIANG and his wife who
lived in Shanghai with YU YUNG LI at the corner of Rue du
Marche-Pere Proo, and WANG TSE WU and LU TSENG TUNG could
reside there.
A week after this removal I met YU YUNG LI and his
mistress on Rue du Moulin, and we dined together. About
July 20, I again went to their abode but they were gone
and I have completely lost trace of them.
At this time I was living at 98 cite Magy (MAGY ALLEYWAY),
Route Magy.
The four persons of whom I have spoken did not know
my address.
Towards the end of July I went to the home of WANG
KING CHENG (王景成), of whom I have spoken. He told me
that CHENG LING was on his way back to Shanghai and that
the four others had left for Yungkang. Doubting this
information I sent a letter to YU YUNG LI requesting
confirmation of this statement.
Three days later I received a reply from YU YUNG LI,
confirming the departure of WANG FENG HSIANG, WANG TSE HU
and LU TSENG TUNG; he also made mention of the fact that
he had received a communication from the Yungkang Military
Committee, stating that new events had happened necessitat-
ing the presence of WANG FENG HSIANG. This letter was
sent to YU YUNG LI by CHENG LING on his return to Shanghai.
With the reception of this letter I left for Yungkang
on July 29, 1936.
I proceeded to Yushien, near Yungkang, where I arrived
on August 2, but as I was knocked about by members of the
Peace Preservation Corps I did not continue my journey and
returned to Shanghai on August 6.
I stayed at 7 Yong Foh Li (永福里), Route de Sieyes,
my wife's home.
In April and In October I stayed with my wife on Route
de Sieyes; I had $130 which had been lent me on my last trip
to Yungkang. During these three months I ceased entirely
my political activities, because I was frightened of being
arrested since numerous members of the Yungkang sub-pre-
fectural committee had made their surrender.
I wrote four letters to YU YUNG LI , but only received
one reply - October 17; he advised me to stay quiet and
await better days. This letter was delivered to me through
the medium of WANG CHING CHEN of the Ying Tah Vang Cutlery
Shop, Sinsa Road.
pages.zh:
-, 6 -

他们在上海停留了大约三周。
随着这五人抵达上海，我写了一封信给余永礼（YU YUNG LI），通知他他们已抵沪。
在这些代表抵达三天后，余永礼来到他们的旅馆，在我在场的情况下，有人交给他军事委员会的文件，让他转交给中共中央。余永礼离开了旅馆，我不知道这些文件是否安全送达。
问：你什么时候再次见到余永礼的？
答：在他收到上述文件十天后，我在王凤翔（WANG FENG HSIANG）所住的明乐饭店（Ming Loh Hotel）的一个房间里见到了他，当时他询问如何发送来自中共中央的关于重组上述四个红色支队的文件到永康。我说有一个叫程玲（CHENG LING）的人总是可以承担这项任务。
当天凌晨4点左右，余永礼带来了文件，我把它们交给了程玲，他随即动身前往永康。这些事件发生在六月底和七月初。
在移交这些文件的第二天，余永礼在磨坊路（Rue du Moulin）馨香斋面包店店主家里租了一个房间，以便让与余永礼一同住在普鲁神父路（Rue du Marche-Pere Proo）街角的王凤翔及其妻子，以及王泽武（WANG TSE WU）和卢增东（LU TSENG TUNG）能够住在那里。
在这次搬迁一周后，我在磨坊路遇到了余永礼和他的情妇，我们一起吃了饭。大约在7月20日，我再次去他们的住所，但他们已经走了，我完全失去了他们的踪迹。
当时我住在马吉路（Route Magy）马吉里（cite Magy / MAGY ALLEYWAY）98号。
我提到的那四个人不知道我的地址。
七月下旬，我去了我之前提到的王景成（WANG KING CHENG）家。他告诉我，程玲正在返回上海的路上，而其他四人已经前往永康。我对这一信息表示怀疑，于是给余永礼写了一封信，要求确认这一说法。
三天后，我收到了余永礼的回信，确认了王凤翔、王泽虎（WANG TSE HU）和卢增东的离开；他还提到，他从永康军事委员会收到了一份通讯，称发生了新的事件，需要王凤翔在场。这封信是程玲回到上海后寄给余永礼的。
收到这封信后，我于1936年7月29日前往永康。
我前往永康附近的俞仙（Yushien），于8月2日到达，但由于遭到保安团成员的殴打，我没有继续行程，并于8月6日返回上海。
我住在妻子位于薛华立路（Route de Sieyes）永福里7号的家中。
四月和十月，我和妻子一起住在薛华立路；我有130美元，这是我上次去永康时借给我的。在这三个月里，我完全停止了政治活动，因为我害怕被捕，因为永康县分委会有许多成员已经自首。
我给余永礼写了四封信，但只收到了一封回信——10月17日；他建议我保持安静，等待更好的日子。这封信是通过新闸路（Sinsa Road）英达旺刀剪店（Ying Tah Vang Cutlery Shop）的王敬臣（WANG CHING CHEN）转交给我的。

pages.en:
- 7 -

I must state that WANG is not a communist; he is merely
a simple go-between who is happy if he can make some easy
earned money. He was not au courant with our business.
Q. Under what circumstances have you known TING VI PING
(丁维炳)?
A. I do not know a TING VI PING, but I recall a certain TING
VI MING (丁维炳), who I met in 1929 in the Wuping (武平)
locality. He was unemployed. I had no business with
him and I have not seen him since.
Q. You are accused of the murder of TING VI PING; what about
that?
A. No! That is not true; it is quite possible that it is a
question of TING VI MING, who was really a secret agent of
the Protection Corps. He was killed in April 1936 as
well as another secret agent, in the village of Mutatseng
(木坦镇)(Wuping district), by men of the 3rd. Group of the
1st. detachment. I learnt these details from a report
sent by this detachment to our military committee.
Q. Coming back to your relations with YU YUNG LI, have you
seen him since the reception of his last letter?
A. I saw him the day after - that is to say on October 18;
in this letter he had made a rendezvous with me at Tang
Pou Ghiao (打浦桥)(Port Pere Robert), at about 10 o'clock,
in the evening. I went there and during the interview,
YU YUNG LI requested me to go home immediately as he had
no new information and the meeting place had been badly
chosen to carry on a lengthy interview, as there were so
many people about.
I returned home and since that time have not seen
YU YUNG LI.
At the end of October I met by chance on Rue Falikao
the wife of WANG FENG HSIANG, one LOU SHAO HSIANG (樓少香),
but she would not give me her address, nor any news of her
husband.
On November 7 I was arrested under circumstances of
which you are fully aware.
Q. You realise you are wanted by the Chinese Authorities, who
are asking for your extradition, for communism, robbery,
escape and murder?
A. I have no objection to being handed over to the Chinese
Authorities. I admit that I have been a communist and have
escaped from prison, but I deny deny having committing any
murders.
Q. Have you anything else to say?
A. No.

Statement in Chinese given to the prisoner, who maintained
the veracity of his statement, and signed it with myself
and the interpreter.
pages.zh:
- 7 -

我必须声明，王不是共产党员；他只是一个简单的中间人，只要能赚点轻松的钱他就很高兴。他对我们的事务并不知情。
问：你是在什么情况下认识丁维炳（TING VI PING）的？
答：我不认识丁维炳，但我记得一个叫丁维明（TING VI MING，原文注为丁维炳）的人，我是1929年在武平（Wuping）地区遇到他的。他当时失业。我与他没有业务往来，此后也未再见过他。
问：你被指控谋杀丁维炳，对此你怎么说？
答：不！那不是真的；很有可能是指丁维明，他确实是保卫团的秘密特工。1936年4月，他和另一名秘密特工在武平县木坦镇（Mutatseng）村被第一支队第三组的人员杀害。我是从该支队向我们军事委员会发送的一份报告中得知这些细节的。
问：回到你与余永礼的关系上来，自从收到他的最后一封信后，你见过他吗？
答：我在第二天，也就是10月18日见到了他；在那封信中，他约我晚上10点左右在打浦桥（Tang Pou Ghiao / Port Pere Robert）见面。我去了那里，在会面期间，余永礼要求我立即回家，因为他没有新的消息，而且由于周围人太多，那个地方不适合进行长时间的谈话。
我回到家，从那以后就再也没有见过余永礼。
十月底，我在法租界霞飞路（Rue Falikao）偶然遇到了王凤翔的妻子楼少香（LOU SHAO HSIANG），但她不肯给我她的地址，也不肯透露她丈夫的任何消息。
11月7日，我在你们完全了解的情况下被捕。
问：你意识到中国当局正在通缉你，并要求引渡你，罪名是共产主义、抢劫、越狱和谋杀吗？
答：我不反对被移交给中国当局。我承认我曾是共产党员并曾越狱，但我否认犯有任何谋杀罪。
问：你还有什么要说的吗？
答：没有。

向囚犯宣读的中文陈述，他坚持其陈述的真实性，并与我和翻译员一起签署了该陈述。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 12, 1936

COURT OFFICER IS
HELD AS A RED
Arraigned As Communist
By Alleged Red Leader
Now Facing Trial

Yu Yung-li, an officer of the
Second Special District Court, is
being detained on suspicion of
being a co-worker of a suspected
Communist leader, Li Yang-ching,
who was recently arrested near
the Great World Amusement re-
sort. Li has been brought to trial
in the Third Branch Kiangsu
High Court and in one of the
hearings held on Tuesday he de-
scribed his co-operation with Yu
as Communistic in nature.
Li is alleged to be a notorious
Communist operating in several
districts in Chekiang. He recently
came here secretly and while
walking in the street he was
caught by the joint force of de-
tectives from the French police
and Bureau of Public Safety. Soon
after his arrest he was brought up
in the Third Branch Kiangsu
High Court for trial and remand-
ed in custody after a short hear-
ing. During his detention Li is
alleged to have told the police
that Yu was his accomplice.
Yu was at once detained and a
preliminary hearing was held by
the chief procurator Mr. Chiao
Wan-sh.en. On Tuesday afternoon
both Li and Yu were brought up
for trial. While Li made many
serious allegations against Yu
the latter denied that he had any-
thing to do with Communists.
Framing a counter charge against
Li, Yu told the court that Li
murdered his (Li's) brother in
his native district. After the
murder, he alleged, Li asked him
to join his gang of robbers. Yu
refused to accept the proposal.
Angered by Yu's attitude, Li was
said to have written threatening
letters to him.
Yu's room in the Second Special
District Court building was
searched by the police who found
several letters that might enable
them to obtain more clues.

S.2.

《字林西报》，1936年11月12日，星期四

法院官员被控为赤色分子
被指认为共产党领导人
现正面临审判

第二特区地方法院的一名官员余永礼因涉嫌与最近在大世界游乐场附近被捕的疑似共产党领导人李扬清合作而被拘留。李已在江苏高等法院第三分院受审，在周二举行的一次听证会上，他描述了他与余的合作具有共产主义性质。
据称，李是一名在浙江多个地区活动的臭名昭著的共产党人。他最近秘密来到这里，在街上行走时被法国警察和公安局的联合侦探队伍抓获。被捕后不久，他被带到江苏高等法院第三分院受审，经过简短听证后被还押候审。据称，李在被拘留期间告诉警方，余是他的同伙。
余随即被拘留，首席检察官焦宛生先生主持了初步听证。周二下午，李和余均出庭受审。虽然李对余提出了许多严重指控，但后者否认他与共产党有任何关系。余对李提出反诉，告诉法院李在其家乡杀害了他的（李的）兄弟。据称，谋杀发生后，李邀请余加入他的强盗团伙。余拒绝接受这一提议。据说李因余的态度而愤怒，曾给他写过恐吓信。
警察搜查了余在第二特区地方法院大楼内的房间，发现了几封信件，这可能使他们获得更多线索。

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:

COURT CLERK FOUND TO BE A COMMUNIST

On November 7 Li Yang Ching (李揚敬) alias Chen Kwang Min (陳光明), age 25, native of Chekiang, a member of the Chinese Communist Party, was arrested by the French Police at the corner of Boulevard de Montigny and Tsai Sz Road (菜市路), French Concession. The man was arraigned before the 3rd Branch of the Kiangsu High Court and was ordered to be detained for further investigation.
During the period of remand, accused Li Yang Ching stated that one Yui Yung Li (余永礼), age about 30, native of Chekiang, a clerk of the Shanghai 2nd Special District Court, is his accomplice.
Acting on instructions received from the 3rd Branch of the Kiangsu High Court, Mr. Wong Ss Muh (王思默), President of the 2nd Special District Court, ordered the detention of Yui Yung Li.
At 5.30 p.m. yesterday, the High Court held a hearing. The accused Li Yang Ching and the clerk Yui Yung Li were present.
After an hour's close interrogation, the High Court found Yui Yung Li to be connected with the Communist Party. The accused Li Yang Ching was handed to the French Police for detention, while the accused Yui Yung Li was placed in the Detention House of the Court.

EXTENSIVE PROPAGANDA MOVEMENT AGAINST NARCOTICS

The extensive propaganda movement against narcotics in this locality commenced on the morning of November 10. The Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commissioner's Headquarters has issued a proclamation emphasizing the determination of the government to suppress the narcotics evil and calling upon all persons who use narcotics or who take morphine injections to get rid of their habit before the end of this year. The Bureau of Public Safety is detailing publicity groups, carrying different kinds of propaganda literature, to the various factories and common people's houses to propagate against the narcotic evil. Posters containing slogans on the movement have been posted up by the Bureau of Public Safety on walls at various street intersections to persuade citizens to give up their habits

法院书记员被发现是共产党人

11月7日，李扬清（Li Yang Ching），又名陈光明（Chen Kwang Min），25岁，浙江人，中国共产党党员，在法租界蒙梯尼路（Boulevard de Montigny）与菜市路（Tsai Sz Road）拐角处被法国警察逮捕。该人被提解至江苏高等法院第三分院，并被命令拘留以作进一步调查。
在还押期间，被告李扬清称，余永礼（Yui Yung Li），约30岁，浙江人，上海第二特区地方法院书记员，是他的同伙。
根据江苏高等法院第三分院的指示，第二特区地方法院院长王思默先生下令拘留余永礼。
昨天下午5时30分，高等法院举行听证会。被告李扬清和书记员余永礼出席。
经过一小时的严密审讯，高等法院认定余永礼与共产党有关联。被告李扬清被移交给法国警察拘留，而被告余永礼则被关入法院看守所。
